blocks.text:
This journey is for you if you want to see the region’s main natural and historic sites in comfort. The programme includes Belmond hotels, Casa Gangotena and Mashpi Lodge, private transfers along much of the route, guides, carefully planned journeys and small groups on nature excursions. The trip remains active, with early starts, altitudes of up to 5,200 metres, boats in the Amazon, trains in the Andes, yachts and walking trails on volcanic islands.

The contrasts begin in Peru. From Lima’s Pacific coast, you travel to Iquitos, where the journey largely moves onto the water. A few days later, the humid tropical forest gives way to the Sacred Valley and high-altitude Cusco. In Ecuador, the scenery changes again: the colonial capital at around 2,800 metres, then Mashpi’s humid cloud forest and finally the dry volcanic landscapes of the Galápagos Islands. This journey brings different parts of South America into one continuous programme, with flights, boats, trains and road transfers arranged for you.

Machu Picchu and Cusco reveal the heritage of the Incas, the Amazon gives you several days among rivers and tropical forest, and the Galápagos offer opportunities to observe animals just a few steps away. Between these sections, you visit Lima and the Larco Museum, colonial Quito, the equator and a cloud forest where hundreds of bird species live among ferns and orchids.

Each major nature experience has several days, rather than a brief stop. The Amazon section includes the cruise and excursions into Pacaya-Samiria, Mashpi includes the lodge’s three-day programme, and the Galápagos include a journey across Santa Cruz and two full days at sea. There is time to take a boat into narrow waterways, walk a forest trail, climb a volcanic island and spend several hours at Machu Picchu. The city visits also go beyond a sightseeing drive: Lima includes a separate visit to the Larco Museum, Cusco combines archaeological sites with the historic centre, and Quito includes the old town and the equator area.
